subsystems.name: Cortical interface layer
subsystems.role: the physical contact with brain tissue — reading the firing of neurons and writing activity back.
parts: penetrating microelectrode arrays or flexible polymer threads

subsystems.name: Wireless power and data link
subsystems.role: connects the implanted layer to external compute without wires through the skull.

subsystems.name: Neuromorphic co-processor
subsystems.role: a silicon layer that mimics neuron and synapse behaviour to translate between brain signals and machine data.

subsystems.name: Decoding and encoding software
subsystems.role: turns raw spike trains into meaning, and generates stimulation patterns the cortex can read.

subsystems.name: Biocompatible packaging
subsystems.role: keeps salt water, ions and immune cells away from the electronics for years.

subsystems.name: Power supply
subsystems.role: runs the implant without a cable through the skin.

buildSteps.title: Map the cortical circuit
buildSteps.detail: Record and stimulate in animals and in people undergoing surgery to learn what activity patterns correspond to a memory or a movement.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the electrode array
buildSteps.detail: Thin-film polymer threads carrying hundreds of micron-scale electrodes are patterned in a cleanroom, so the array bends with the brain instead of cutting it.

buildSteps.title: Make the neuromorphic chip
buildSteps.detail: Silicon or memristive circuits are designed so their dynamics resemble real synapses — this is the 'overlay' layer itself.

buildSteps.title: Package it for the body
buildSteps.detail: The chip and electronics are sealed in a flexible, hermetic shell that survives years of warm, salty, immune-active tissue.

buildSteps.title: Implant
buildSteps.detail: Surgeons place the array on or into the cortex; research is also exploring routes through blood vessels to avoid opening the skull.

buildSteps.title: Close the loop
buildSteps.detail: The decoder is trained on the individual's own signals until the chip's output is intelligible to their brain, and vice versa.

buildSteps.title: Add the wireless link
buildSteps.detail: Power and data are transmitted through the skin, allowing the implant to talk to a wearable or external processor.

buildSteps.title: Co-adapt over time
buildSteps.detail: The user and the system learn each other — the plasticity that would theoretically let extra memory or processing be usable rather than foreign.

prerequisites.why: arrays in clinical research record from around a hundred neurons and degrade over months to a few years; an overlay would need thousands over a decade.
speech and movement have been decoded from human cortex in small trials, but general memory and reasoning have not.
stimulation can evoke percepts and has been used experimentally to improve recall, but the neural code for complex thought is unknown.

prerequisites.tech: Wireless power and data at depth
prerequisites.why: millimetre-scale free-floating 'neural dust' has been proposed and modelled; getting power and bandwidth through tissue to many nodes is unsolved.
chips exist that emulate millions of neurons, but matching a living cortex in a body-safe package is far off.
we know memories are distributed and replayed, not stored in one place, so there is no known format to plug an overlay into.

pathway.milestone: clinical brain-computer interfaces restore communication and cursor control for a small number of paralysed people
pathway.unlocks: proof that cortex can be read and written in humans safely enough for research.

pathway.milestone: wireless implants with thousands of stable channels and multi-year lifetimes
pathway.unlocks: everyday use without a plug through the skull, and enough data to build real decoders.

pathway.milestone: closed-loop bidirectional systems that write patterns as fluently as they read them
pathway.unlocks: experimental memory and sensory prosthetics, first for injury and disease.

pathway.milestone: an external co-processor that a person can query as if it were part of their own cognition
pathway.unlocks: the functions the tile describes — expanded working memory, parallel streams of thought, faster skill learning.

pathway.milestone: a true synaptic bridge, where silicon and biological synapses adapt to each other continuously
pathway.unlocks: cognitive augmentation beyond restoration — with unresolved questions of identity, consent and access.
